title: Find Reachability
body:
Members of a developer network follow each other. An edge u v means u follows v, and information flows from u to v along that direction.

A JS newbie A wants to know whether he can reach the React expert B through the network. Print 1 if there is a directed path from A to B, otherwise 0. A member always reaches themself.

Function to complete

Complete canReach(members, follower, following, a, b). It returns 1 if A can reach B, otherwise 0.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: Line 1: N. Line 2: the N member IDs. Line 3: E. Next E lines: an edge. Last line: A B. Each edge is follower following.
cons: Member IDs are integers without spaces

samples.ex: Nobody follows 7, so starting from 5 you can never get to 7.

lc: 1971 Find if Path Exists in Graph

py.pre:
from typing import *
import sys, math, collections, heapq, bisect, itertools, functools
from collections import *
py.post:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    _n = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    members = list(map(int, _t[_p:_p + (_n)])); _p += (_n)
    _e = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    follower = []; following = []
    for _ in range((_e)):
        follower.append(int(_t[_p + 0]))
        following.append(int(_t[_p + 1]))
        _p += 2
    a = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    b = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    _r = Solution().canReach(members, follower, following, a, b)
    print(_r)
